title: Plans to move FBI headquarters to Reagan Building blocked by federal judge
summary: A federal judge in Maryland ruled that the Trump administration's decision to move the FBI headquarters to the Ronald Reagan Building runs counter to spending bills passed by Congress.

title: Social Security expands electronic health record sharing to speed up disability claims adjudication
summary: A health data sharing superhighway “allows SSA to access complete, structured medical records within seconds or minutes for claimants, helping to significantly reduce disability claim processing times,” an agency official told Nextgov/FCW.

title: Attorney general violated Hatch Act ethics rules, nonprofit says
summary: Good government groups have filed Hatch Act complaints against several Trump administration officials.

title: USDA hasn’t looked at staff attrition ahead of relocations, but downplays its impact
summary: Internal data shows the department is preparing for significant churn as it presses forward with office moves, raising questions about whether new staff can fill the gap left by seasoned experts.

title: Getting a simple FOIA request from OPM shouldn’t be this hard
summary: COMMENTARY | A frequent FOIA requester found himself navigating dead inboxes, broken portals and months-long waits after cuts gutted the Office of Personnel Management’s public records operation.

title: Bill expanding paid leave for feds is pared back in Senate
summary: The upper chamber’s version of legislation extending 12 weeks of paid family leave each year to federal workers removes provisions allowing it to be used in connection with helping a family member who has been the victim of sexual assault, domestic violence or stalking.

title: National crisis and support hotline operations remained consistent despite staffing cuts, watchdog found
summary: Some staff operating mental health support hotlines at the departments of Health and Human Services and Veterans Affairs were subject to reductions in force last year and have not yet been replaced.

title: EPA’s cancer-risk data has gone dark
summary: The agency is still publishing air pollution data, but a key part of its analysis is missing from the latest release.

title: The Army gave General Dynamics $533M to build an artillery plant that produced nothing
summary: Instead of making shells, the assembly robots kept failing in bizarre ways—and that's just for starters.

title: Labor looks to AI to tackle accommodation requests from disabled employees
summary: Employees say they’ve waited months or longer for decisions, as the Labor Department considers using AI to sort requests and flag missing documentation.

title: OneGov savings balloon to over $1.6B as agencies weigh future of AI in contracting
summary: The General Services Administration has already agreed to extend some OneGov deals and is working on brokering new ones, according to an official.

title: OPM finalizes expanded hazard pay for federal firefighters
summary: Under regulations set to take effect next month, federal wildland firefighters will be eligible for 25% hazard pay in connection with work on prescribed burns.

title: Intel ops are underway at Space Command’s nascent Alabama HQ
summary: Alabama landed SPACECOM after a years-long political fight. Now it’s getting off the ground.

title: Lawsuit seeks to enforce 2025 SCOTUS decision improving pay for feds called to active duty
summary: In the 15 months since the Supreme Court ruled that federal workers who also serve as military reservists do not need to prove that an active duty deployment is “substantially connected” to a national emergency, OPM has yet to issue new guidance reflecting the new precedent.

title: Before you take money out of your TSP, weigh these trade-offs
summary: A withdrawal can affect everything from your tax bill and Medicare premiums to how long your savings last and what your heirs receive.

title: The feds want private companies to take the fight to cybercriminals
summary: A new program would put vetted companies in a more active role against transnational criminal groups, with DHS and Justice overseeing the operations.

title: Statistical agency staffing cuts put federal data under new scrutiny on Capitol Hill
summary: House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Bobby Scott, D-Va., is pressing for a September hearing to examine what staffing losses and leadership vacancies mean for agencies responsible for producing key data.

title: State’s overseas housing rules haven’t kept up with the times, GAO says
summary: The agency is still using standards tied to the D.C. housing market of 1991 to determine how much space employees stationed abroad can have.

title: State Department expands push to reclassify employees as at-will workers
summary: An expanded search for more Schedule Policy/Career conversions is still in its early stages, but a department employee says the effort is “moving relatively fast.”

title: Space Command says it needs to ‘shoot, move and communicate’ in orbit
summary: Gen. Stephen Whiting, the outgoing commander of U.S. Space Command, used his final speech at the Space and Missile Defense Symposium in Huntsville, Ala., to outline the capabilities he says the military needs to keep pace with China.

title: Federal agencies are looking beyond the usual sources for new ideas
summary: NIH is offering $1 million for practical ideas that could help long-acting HIV prevention and treatment reach more people, and applicants do not need a traditional research background to participate.

title: VA’s benefits system overhaul is running into some familiar problems
summary: An audit found gaps in planning, cost estimates and oversight that could put the modernization effort further behind schedule.

title: NTEU sets deadline for its members to resume paying dues
summary: The union’s deadline comes as the Trump administration has stripped collective bargaining rights from roughly two-thirds of NTEU members and disrupted its primary source of revenue.

title: IRS says a new policy ‘moots’ NTEU’s First Amendment lawsuit. The union isn’t so sure
summary: A new policy allows only “agency-sponsored materials” to be posted on communal office bulletin boards, but agency officials still say they have discretion to approve or deny other documents.
